For an arbitrary aggregate function without nice properties, it is difficult to improve beyond an exhaustive algorithm that enumerates and evaluates all possible predicates.
This algorithm is inefficient because the number of single-attribute clauses increases exponentially (quadratically) for a discrete (continuous) attribute as its cardinality increases.
Additionally, the space of possible conjunctions is exponential with the number of attributes. The combination of the two issues makes the problem untenable for even small datasets.
